question: A can do a work in 9 days and B can do the same work in 21 days. If they work on it together for 2 days, then what fraction of the work is left?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Total Work = LCM(9, 21) = 63 units.

Efficiency of A = 63 ÷ 9 = 7 units/day.

Efficiency of B = 63 ÷ 21 = 3 units/day.

Work done together in 2 days = (7 + 3) × 2 = 20 units.

Remaining work = 63 − 20 = 43 units.

**∴ The correct answer is 43/63.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A = 9 days

Time taken by B = 21 days

Time they worked together = 2 days

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total combined efficiency of A and B = 7 + 3 = 10 units/day.

⇒ Total work done by them in 2 days = 10 × 2 = 20 units.

⇒ Work left to be done = Total Work − Work completed

⇒ Work left = 63 − 20 = 43 units.

⇒ Fraction of work left = Remaining Work ÷ Total Work

⇒ Fraction of work left = 43/63

**∴ The correct answer is 43/63.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Work using LCM Method

Total work can be assumed as the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the time taken by all individuals. This ensures the calculated efficiencies are integers, completely avoiding complex fractional calculations.

Work done by (A + B) together

If A can do a piece of work in x days and B can do the same work in y days, then working together they can complete the whole work in (x × y) / (x + y) days.

Work Left or Dropping Out Mid-way

When someone leaves early, always calculate the total work completed until they left using their combined efficiency. Then subtract it from the total work to get the remaining work.
